body.text: In short:
An undisclosed honorary membership to the Marrickville Golf Club given to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese granted the same access as an annual membership, worth $1,100, not $5 as Mr Albanese claimed.
The club's management also said the $6.05 million grant value was based on a "guesstimate" of what its proposed upgrades would cost.
What's next?
An inquiry into the grants program under which the golf club was funded is continuing.

Marrickville Golf Club's management says the honorary membership it gifted Prime Minister Anthony Albanese granted full access, the same as its $1,100 annual memberships — far more than the $5 social membership Mr Albanese claimed he was conferred.
The club's management also admitted the $6.05 million grant it was awarded by Mr Albanese was never intended to fund sewerage fixes, which are being done under a separate NSW grant.

Earlier this month, Mr Albanese conceded he was wrong when he told the House of Representatives that the grant he had promised the Marrickville Golf Club at the 2025 election was to stop septic tank sewage flooding into the river.
"When it floods in Marrickville, raw sewage flows into the Cooks River. That is what the funding is for," Mr Albanese told the House of Representatives in September.
General manager Mathew Ward, however, said sewerage upgrades were never part of the federal grant.

"I think that's basically correct … we were very optimistic about the prospects of the [NSW] grant. Certainly that was one of the leading issues we brought to [Mr Albanese's] electorate office," he said.
"It was not ultimately part of what was funded with the $6.05 million."
Mr Ward said that sewerage issues had been raised with Mr Albanese's electorate office as its leading concern, in the event that its pending application for state grant funding was unsuccessful.
Mr Ward said the grant had come about after the club had approached Mr Albanese's electorate office with proposed fixes, and was invited in return to put forward other upgrade ideas it might have.

Mr Ward returned with a "bundle of ideas" in November 2024, which, beyond a $1 million stormwater harvesting upgrade, he said he had costed at $6.05 million based on "a bit of an educated guesstimate".
"[It was] purely my estimates based on a combination of my experience of renovations at golf clubs," Mr Ward said.
The general manager noted after the club had been invited to apply for that funding, it commissioned "very detailed" professional costings.
Frontbench minister Murray Watt said the golf club grant "along with many others" was a standard election commitment.

"The way those processes work, I have been through them many times myself, is that community organisations put forward requests to members and candidates for community facilities like this. They provide their best estimate of what that will cost," Senator Watt said.
"But one of the things we do is undertake a value for money test after the election to ensure value for money is being provided."
Club reveals honorary member rights same as $1,100 membership
Mr Albanese made the claims in the chamber that the grant was for sewerage fixes under scrutiny over his undisclosed honorary membership, revealed by the ABC.
The prime minister said that same day the membership was worth just $5 for two years.
"If anyone wants to join what is affectionately known as Royal Marrickville, what they need for two years' membership is $5," Mr Albanese told the House of Representatives.
"I don't have a card, I don't go in there, I haven't been in there for years."

The club's management said it had three membership types: a social membership worth $5 for two years, golfing membership worth $1,100 a year and honorary membership, which grants all the rights of a golfing member.
The conferral of Mr Albanese's honorary membership also led to the creation of a golfing account for him in national handicapping service GOLF Link, now Golf Australia CONNECT.
The club's management said Mr Albanese's membership had been entered into its database without accompanying public notification or acknowledgement by the board at the time.
"Conventionally you only give it to people who never use it," Mr Ward joked.

The prime minister has received golfing lessons from the Marrickville Golf Club's head professional, but the club confirmed there were no entries under his honorary membership since it was granted in 2012.
"This was an honorary membership that the prime minister was not even aware that he had, and once he became aware of it he rescinded that honorary membership," Senator Watt said.
Mr Albanese wrote to the golf club to formally decline his membership following the ABC's report.

The Marrickville Golf Club is well known as one of the most affordable city golf courses in the country, and is a community hub for events in Sydney's inner west, as well as a popular cycling and walking spot — including for Mr Albanese, who used to walk his dog Toto there regularly when he lived next door.
Mr Ward said the club had suffered verbal abuse from strangers since revelations of the prime minister's honorary membership, saying its bar staff had been forced to switch off its phones at times.
"It is a little bit disappointing when smart alecs ring up our dear bar staff and ask for their 'Albo money' back," Mr Ward said.
"From the club's perspective I am confident we have behaved in a way we always will, which is proper and ethical."

The club's management said it had no contact with Mr Albanese in relation to reporting on his membership, and its only contact with his electorate office in recent weeks had been in order to inquire into what would be expected of them at their appearance at the ongoing senate inquiry into the program.

Separately, the national audit office confirmed to the inquiry it believed there was "merit" in further scrutinising the grants scheme, which has been listed as a possible audit option for this financial year.
Opposition Leader Angus Taylor accused the prime minister of lying to parliament about the grant's purpose and his honorary membership.
“The prime minister has been caught out telling more lies about his dodgy $6 million grant to Marrickville Golf Club," he said.
In September, Mr Albanese tried to tell parliament his undisclosed honorary membership was worth $5.
Today, Marrickville Golf Club confirmed to parliament it was worth $1,100.
“Anthony Albanese lied about the grant being for sewerage, he lied about the grant being invitation-only, and he lied about the value of his secret membership,” Mr Taylor wrote on social media.
“He just can’t bring himself to tell the truth and take responsibility.”
